# Tokenization

*Concept* · also written tokenisation

Splitting text into tokens (words or word parts) for the index or for an AI model.

**Glossary** (*Tokenization*): Splitting text into small units. Google Search stores words (tokens) with metadata, while AI models split text into sub-word pieces mapped to numeric IDs.

Narrative: the topic [Tokenization: how text is stored](../topics/tokenization.md) tells the story; this card lists what links to it.

9 claims mention it: 7 shown or said at the event (5 not in Google docs, 2 consistent with Google docs), 2 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [Understand and count tokens](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/tokens).

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D2-C319`](../sessions/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: For languages written with spaces between words, such as English and German, Search tokenization splits a sentence into its individual words. `[D2-C319, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C325`](../sessions/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: Tokenization for AI models such as Gemini, in training and in inference, differs from tokenization for Search, although Gary Illyes qualified this with 'or mostly'. `[D2-C325, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C328`](../sessions/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) Slide, Day 2, not in Google docs: Google's two tokenization slides showed the difference on the same sentence: the Search tokenizer kept 'robots.txt' and 'tl;dr' as single tokens, while the AI-model tokenizer split them into pieces such as 'tl' and 'dr' or 'robots' and 'txt', with the punctuation as separate tokens. `[D2-C328, slide, Gary Illyes, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C720`](../sessions/D2-S23-how-does-the-index-look-like.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: Google's Search index stores the tokens produced by tokenizing each page, as they are, together with the metadata attached to the tokens during tokenization. `[D2-C720, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D3-C108`](../sessions/D3-S04-lightning-session-k-facets-of-quality.md) Stage, Day 3, not in Google docs: A community speaker compared Googlebot to an inspector who cannot enter the shop and only looks through the window, seeing the page as ones and zeros, which the speaker linked to tokenization. `[D3-C108, stage, a community speaker, Day 3]`
- [`D1-C039`](../sessions/D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md) Slide, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: Gemini is not part of Search, but it uses crawlers for data, shares some technologies such as tokenization and deduping, and grounds on the Search index. `[D1-C039, slide, Google, Day 1]`
- [`D2-C326`](../sessions/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) Slide, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: In tokenization for AI models, common English words stay whole and each maps to a numeric token ID, so the model works with IDs rather than with the words; on Google's slide the word 'can' had the same ID, 740, both times it appeared. `[D2-C326, slide, Gary Illyes, Day 2]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D2-C329`](../sessions/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) Analysis: Day 1's slide said Gemini shares technologies such as tokenization with Search, while on Day 2 Gary Illyes showed that the two tokenizers split the same text differently ('or mostly'); read this as a shared processing step with different outputs, so Search's word tokens and Gemini's sub-word tokens are not the same units. `[D2-C329, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D3-C109`](../sessions/D3-S04-lightning-session-k-facets-of-quality.md) Analysis: The inspector metaphor blends two steps: Googlebot fetches pages during crawling, while tokenization happens later when the page is processed for the index, as Google explained on Day 2. `[D3-C109, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
